Class DiaryEntryTypeAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.google.gson.TypeAdapter<DiaryEntry>
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.DiaryEntryTypeAdapter
public class DiaryEntryTypeAdapter extends com.google.gson.TypeAdapter<DiaryEntry>
A custom TypeAdapter for serialising and deserialising DiaryEntry objects using Gson.

Role and Responsibility

The DiaryEntryTypeAdapter is required bacause LocalDateTime is not natively supported by Gson, and because Author must be explicitly written and reconstructed. The adapter writes each DiaryEntry to a JSON file as an object and reconstructs it by reading those fields back in the same format, ensuring that entries can be reliably persisted and restored across application sessions.

Information Stored and Data Type Justification

Thos class serialises four fields:

  • Title: Stored as a String in order to be readable and to ensure the exact user input is saved.
  • Author: Stored as a JSON object, containing the authors name. This allows for later modifications.
  • Content: Stored as a String in order to be readable and to ensure the exact user input is saved.
  • Date: Stored as a ISO-8601 String, YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000000. The T separates date from time. Then there are houres, minutes, seconds, and microseconds. This ensures a standarised format.
Mutability Assessment

The adapter is immutable because its only field the DateTimeFormatter is both static and final and thus cannot change. It does not keep any links to objects outside the class, and anything it creates while reading or writing is temporary and thrown away afterwards.This makes the adapter safe to use in several threads at the same time.

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

When encountering malformed or unexpected JSON input, the adapter follows a “best-effort reconstruction” strategy:

  • Unknown fields are skipped using skipValue(), preventing failures caused by forward-compatible schema changes.
  • Missing fields result in null values being passed to the DiaryEntry constructor. It is the responsibility of the constructor or calling logic to validate or reject such entries.
  • Malformed LocalDateTime values produce a parsing exception, which is propagated as an IOException, signalling to the caller that the JSON is not recoverable.

This approach ensures resilience to minor format variations while still surfacing genuinely invalid or corrupted data.

AI Usage

This class was created with guidance from an AI tool to resolve the issue of Gson not automatically supporting the LocalDateTime format. The implementation has since been reviewed and adapted to suit the evolving design and requirements of the application.
